correctness.rationale: PASS: Let P_m(n) be coefficients of the m-th product term. Expansion in y=e^{−t}−1 with integral coefficients divisible by y^m implies m!|P_m(n), uniformly truncating m≥3r modulo 3^r. For m<3r inclusion-exclusion expresses terms as sums of K_S^n and Euler/Carmichael periodicity gives eventual period 2·3^{r−1}. For r≥2, normalized first-third-shift at h=2·3^{r−2} depends on K_S modulo 9; the factor with 2j−1=9 (j=5) pairs/cancels all m≥5. Exact m≤4 subset sums produce residue 2 for even n and zero for odd. Modulo three a(n) alternates, so all eventual periods are even; the nonzero first-third shift excludes all proper divisors. Independent dual coefficient recurrences plus direct subset-residue check corroborated r=1..4 at tested indices, not the infinite statement.
